title: Unemployment Benefit Claims Dependency Allowance Rates
content:
For each program of Unemployment Benefit Claims, the program's dependency allowance per dependent is the weekly amount added per eligible dependent, and the maximum number of dependents is the most dependents for which an allowance is paid.

| Program | Dependency allowance per dependent (USD per week per dependent) | Maximum number of dependents for which an allowance is paid |
|---|---|---|
| Regular State Unemployment Insurance | 15.00 | 3 |
| Unemployment Compensation for Federal Employees (UCFE) | 15.00 | 3 |
| Unemployment Compensation for Ex-Servicemembers (UCX) | 15.00 | 3 |
| Combined Wage Claim (CWC) | 15.00 | 3 |
| Extended Benefits (EB) | 15.00 | 3 |
| Trade Readjustment Allowances (TRA) | 15.00 | 3 |
| Disaster Unemployment Assistance (DUA) | 0.00 | 0 |

### Points read from the table

**Is a dependency allowance paid on a Disaster Unemployment Assistance (DUA) claim?** The program's per-dependent figure is 0.00 and its maximum number of dependents is 0, so the schedule provides no dependency allowance for that program.

**What is the largest weekly allowance the per-dependent figure reaches on a Regular State Unemployment Insurance claim?** With the per-dependent figure of 15.00 and no more than 3 dependents counted, the product of the two is 45.00 per week (a derivation from the two table entries).
